text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High GPU memory paging + transient OOMs observed on runtime pool 'prod-us-east-1' affecting text-generation endpoints. Trigger: GPU memory paging > 80% and 5 OOMs in 10m. Incident link: https://redwood.incidents/1887654321

Elena: I'm oncall. Acknowledging. Jon, can you take lead on mitigation? tagging SRE rotation.

Jon: taking lead. Quick checklist: 1) reduce batch_size on hot routes, 2) route traffic to fallback variant, 3) collect GPU mem stats & dmesg, 4) coordinate customer impact. I'll start with (1).

Amy: adding context from runtime: we've seen repeated NVLINK/page-fault spikes when kv-cache growth is uneven across sequences. Hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + large variable seq lengths causing inefficient allocation -> host paging.

Jon: on it. Rolling a quick per-route override to lower batch size for /v1/generate on model redwood-large-prod: ```
# reduce batch size for route
redwood routes update /v1/generate --model redwood-large-prod --override "batch_size=8"
```

April: support looking now — two enterprise customers reported increased 500s around 12:14UTC, ticket IDs: S-8931, S-8932. Both hit during long-prompt jobs. Will draft an interim status if we have ETA.

Kevin: infra note: some nodes hit host memory pressure due to GPU pinned allocations + kernel page faults. I can temporarily increase node-level reserved memory for GPU drivers to reduce host OOM, but that won't fix fragmentation. Suggest routing to quantized fallback while we investigate.

Jon: executing fallback route switch: ```
# switch traffic to quantized variant
redwood routing set --model redwood-large-prod --fallback redwood-large-quant-2x --weight 100
```

SRE-Assistant: Aggregated logs & metrics: https://logs.redwood/1887654321/ (GPU mem curves, nv-host page faults, kvcache sizes). Uploaded small sample of OOM stacktrace: ```
[OOM] runtime.cpp:243 allocate failed len=10485760 free=5242880
kv_cache.cpp:line 112 free segments: 12 used: 140 shards:128
nvml: page_faults=735
```

Amy: quick theory checklist in-thread: - KV cache shard count too high -> small free fragments across many shards - Large batch + long seq combos amplify allocation path - Some models have warm KV caches from long prefixes (restarts) causing uneven growth. Proposed actions: reduce kv_cache_shards to 64 for affected model, enable eager compaction on next config push, and lower default per-request kv reserve from 2MB -> 1MB.

Jon: creating an actionable timeline. Everyone drop logs for these windows: 12:05-12:20UTC and 12:30-12:40UTC. I'll compile.

Elena: customer impact: April, are there any paid SLO breaches? approximate error rate?

April: preliminary: 0.9% overall error spike for the last 15m on /generate for two orgs (both enterprise). No credit-level SLO yet but they hit increased latency/5xxs. I'll prepare a short customer note: "Mitigations in place; working on root cause; ETA TBD".

Kevin: quick mitigation applied: bumped gpu-driver-reserved to 1.2GB on nodes with repeated page faults. That reduced host OOMs but paging persisted. Command run: ```
# host-side tweak
infractl node update --label gpu=true --set gpu_driver_reserved=1.2GB
```

Jon: observed immediate drop in host OOMs after Kevin's tweak, but GPU nvml page_faults still rising. Fallback routing is live, batch_size overrides applied. CPU fallback and quantized variants are taking ~30% of traffic.

Amy: I'm going to attempt an in-memory kv compaction on one canary node to validate compaction helps. Will run compaction script and report memory delta. Command: ```
# on runtime node
./kv_compact --model redwood-large-prod --shards 0-15 --dry-run
```

SRE-Assistant: compaction dry-run output attached: "estimated reclaimable memory: 1.8GB across selected shards". Link: https://artifacts.redwood/kv-compact/dryrun-1887654321.log

Jon: good. If compaction reclaims ~2GB, that'd be viable short-term. Amy, after dry-run, try live compaction on one node (staggered) and monitor.

Amy: live compaction scheduled now on node runtime-ix-07, will run per-shard with 30s pause between.

Elena: handoff note — I'm available but handing lead to Jon for next hour. If we have customer comms, coordinate with April.

Jon: doing live compaction: logs show memory freed ~1.7GB on node runtime-ix-07. nvml page_faults for that node dropped from 420 -> 60 in 5m. Looks promising.

April: drafting customer note: "We've applied mitigations (routing to fallback, reduced batch sizes, compaction) and are monitoring. Next update in 60 minutes or sooner if status changes." Sending to S-8931/S-8932 now.

Kevin: next infra task: evaluate lowering nvlink page-fault threshold and enable driver-level eager reclamation where safe. Opening infra ticket INF-1292.

Amy: config changes I'd recommend for model rollout: ```
model_config:
  kv_cache_shards: 64
  kv_compaction: enabled
  per_request_kv_reserve: 1MB
  default_batch_size: 8
``` Plan: stage to canary, validate no perf regression, then promote.

Jon: documenting hypotheses in-thread: H1: KV cache fragmentation -> host paging -> transient OOMs. H2: specific large prompts caused burst allocations that exposed fragmentation. H3: driver/host memory tuning reduced host OOM but not root fragmentation. Please react with :thumbsup: for H1 if you agree, :thinking: for need more data.

Elena: :thumbsup: for H1. Good notes.

Kevin: :thumbsup: for H1 and :thumbsup: for driver tuning as stopgap.

April: :thinking: for H2 until we confirm prompt-length correlation per org. I'll attach user request IDs.

SRE-Assistant: Collated artifacts: metrics dashboard, compaction logs, routing diff, and the OOM samples: https://incidents.redwood/1887654321/artifacts.zip

Jon: short-term mitigation status: fallback routing 100% -> quantized output for new requests; batch override applied; compaction reclaimed memory on canary nodes; monitoring for regression. Next steps: push model config change to 2 canaries, run load test, then promote.

Amy: I'll prepare a follow-up change PR for kv shards + compaction with perf benchmarks.

Elena: thanks team. Jon, keep me posted at handoff end (in 40m). April, please keep customers updated every 60m. I'll update incident record with timeline and hypothesis votes.

Jon: will do. Closing live mitigation loop now; moving to RCA -> assign owners for postmortem. Owners: Jon (timeline & infra actions), Amy (runtime root cause & config), Kevin (driver/infra changes), April (customer comms).

SRE-Assistant: Incident state: Mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem templated and assigned. Link: https://postmortems.redwood/1887654321

Elena: handoff complete; leaving channel but reachable if needed.

Jon: thanks all. I'll post a first-pass timeline and artifact links in the postmortem within 2 hrs.

April: customers acknowledged interim note and appreciate the quick response. I'll close tickets when RCA summary is ready. :white_check_mark:

Amy: logging action items into runtime backlog: RUNTIME-452 (kv compaction automation), RUNTIME-453 (shard default tuning).

Kevin: infra tasks: INF-1292 (driver reclamation), INF-1293 (node reserved mem tuning doc).

Jon: end of thread for live mitigation. Continuing RCA in postmortem doc.
